edges.description: Rapidly proliferating renal rhabdoid tumor produces a palpable abdominal or flank mass in infancy.
Renal parenchymal and collecting-system invasion by proliferating RTK cells causes gross or microscopic hematuria.
Unchecked proliferation of extrarenal malignant rhabdoid tumor cells in axial or extremity soft tissues presents as an enlarging soft-tissue mass.
Rapid intracranial rhabdoid tumor growth in the AT/RT subtype produces mass effect and obstructive hydrocephalus, causing headache.
Intracranial mass effect and ventricular obstruction from CNS rhabdoid tumor growth elevate intracranial pressure and trigger vomiting.
Complete loss of nuclear INI1/BAF47 immunoreactivity in neoplastic cells serves as the primary tissue readout of biallelic SMARCB1 loss.
Loss of nuclear BRG1 immunoreactivity identifies the rare SMARCA4-deficient arm of the rhabdoid tumor spectrum when INI1 expression is preserved.

nodes.description: Unchecked G1-S progression and EZH1/EZH2 activity sustain rapid malignant rhabdoid tumor proliferation, producing space-occupying renal, soft-tissue, and intracranial masses with local invasion and raised intracranial pressure depending on primary anatomic site.

nodes.description: SMARCB1-deficient rhabdoid tumor cells are maintained in an undifferentiated state, and EZH2 inhibition can trigger differentiation.

nodes.description: Without p16(INK4a) restraint, CDK4-Cyclin D1 kinase activity is left unopposed, driving RB1 phosphorylation and inactivation, and bypassing the G1-S restriction point. Cyclin D1 is the critical downstream effector: its genetic ablation fully abrogates rhabdoid tumorigenesis caused by SMARCB1/Ini1 loss in vivo.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic ablation of Cyclin D1 abrogates genesis of rhabdoid tumors resulting from Ini1 loss.
evidence.snippet: We crossed Ini1+/- mice to Cyclin D1-/- mice and found that Ini1+/- mice with Cyclin D1 deficiency did not develop any spontaneous tumors, in contrast to the parental Ini1+/- mice.

nodes.description: SMARCB1 loss removes its direct transcriptional support for CDKN2A/p16(INK4a) expression, while unopposed PRC2/EZH2 activity further enforces epigenetic silencing of the locus. The net effect is loss of p16(INK4a) protein, which normally restrains CDK4-Cyclin D1 kinase activity.

evidence.reference_title: P16INK4a is required for hSNF5 chromatin remodeler-induced cellular senescence in malignant rhabdoid tumor cells.
evidence.snippet: Following hSNF5 expression, we observed transcriptional activation of the tumor suppressor p16(INK4a) but not of p14(ARF), repression of several cyclins and CD44, a cell surface glycoprotein implicated in metastasis.

nodes.description: EZH2-targeted therapy is an investigational mechanism-based strategy for relapsed or refractory SMARCB1/SMARCA4-deficient disease. Preclinical data support strong EZH2 dependence, and pediatric phase II trials have evaluated tazemetostat in molecularly selected tumors with prolonged disease stabilization in a subset of patients.

evidence.reference_title: Durable tumor regression in genetically altered malignant rhabdoid tumors by inhibition of methyltransferase EZH2.
evidence.snippet: These data demonstrate the dependency of SMARCB1 mutant MRTs on EZH2 enzymatic activity and portend the utility of EZH2-targeted drugs for the treatment of these genetically defined cancers.

evidence.reference_title: Tazemetostat for tumors harboring SMARCB1/SMARCA4 or EZH2 alterations: results from NCI-COG pediatric MATCH APEC1621C.
evidence.snippet: Although tazemetostat did not meet its primary efficacy endpoint in this population of refractory pediatric tumors (objective response rate = 5%, 90% CI = 1% to 20%), 25% of patients with multiple histologic diagnoses experienced prolonged stable disease of 6 months and over (range = 9-26 cycles), suggesting a potential effect of tazemetostat on disease stabilization.

evidence.snippet: It is a heterogeneous group of aggressive tumours with distinct histopathological and immunohistochemistry findings. The tumour is characterised by diffuse proliferation of rhabdoid cells with hyaline like inclusion bodies. Defining feature is aberration of INI1/SMARCB1 gene located at chromosome 22q11.2.
